corpse: Use case: precise-object-edit / identity-preserve. Asset: individual transparent 2D game corpse sprite for Emergency Shift, top-down orthographic camera looking straight down (90 degrees), square canvas. Input image 1 is the exact living creature reference and identity/style source. Make a DEAD REMAINS VARIANT of this same fictional nonhuman creature. Preserve its smooth broad simplified gray-purple flesh, compact torso, tiny featureless lowered damaged head pointing LEFT, two long front arms and two short rear legs. Exactly THREE curved ivory claws on EACH front hand, THREE main claws plus ONE lateral spur on EACH hind foot; do not invent extra hands, fingers, eyes, mouths or heads. Keep the painted broad gradients and low micro-detail of this source; no busy veins, scales or noisy repetitive wrinkles. Death should read clearly as collapsed limp flattened tissue against the floor, not a living crouch. Blood is dark burgundy/red on tissue and torn edges. Slightly darker and more desaturated than the living reference while still readable. Fixed overhead viewpoint and similar character scale; torso/pelvis center around x=60%, y=50%. Full complete silhouette with about 7% transparent padding, nothing clipped. Genuine transparent background, NO floor, no cast shadow, no large ground blood pool, no checkerboard, no text or labels, no panels or multiple alternative designs in one image. Small attached blood smears are fine. All materials should look like the same creature. No human corpse or clothing. VARIANT A, BLOODY COLLAPSED CARCASS: one mostly intact recognizable creature lying belly-down, all four limbs attached. The torso is sagging and visibly flattened, the small head rests on the floor facing left, relaxed forearms flopped at asymmetric but anatomically coherent bends. Keep the same shoulder/elbow/wrist chain and length relationships, with both three-claw front hands clearly identifiable. A broad localized dark torn wound across the left shoulder and front flank, blood smears around the small damaged head; most of the back and claw identity still recognizable. No upright arched alive posture, no posed symmetry.
